protocol: Predictor x scheduler 2x2 for screening, verification and stopping under a fixed budget (executable; NOT FROZEN)
written_at: 2026-10-04 (+0800), parent session, after all exploratory results of this study were seen
status: EXECUTABLE, NOT FROZEN, NOT RUN. Blocked by receipts/phase3_blocking.json (DATA_NOT_QUALIFIED, INSUFFICIENT_UNITS_FOR_TAU). Freeze it (sha256 of protocol, builder and runner; fresh vault log) only after a release passes the data gate on design columns alone.
question: On an untouched, qualified release, does a reproducibility-aware static predictor (historical probability that a candidate is a screen hit AND confirmed by an independent measurement) obtain more independently confirmed discoveries than the screen-label static predictor under the same simple verification scheduler, at equal measurements, wells and rounds; and does an adaptive index scheduler add anything beyond the simple scheduler?
why_this_design: Phase 1 (EXPLORATORY, Jaaks exposed): at an equal feasible budget with carry-over and a terminal verification round, verify-hits beats full-budget paired measurement (+17.7% [13.1, 23.1]) and a development-selected fixed split (+9.1% [5.4, 13.5]), but needs 5 rounds where paired needs 1 and the split 2; at 2 rounds the fixed split wins (-9.1% [-14.3, -3.4] for verify-hits).

Allocation addendum 2 (post hoc): predictor effect under the simple scheduler +6.5% [2.6, 10.6]; scheduler effect -0.8% [-4.0, +2.5] (static predictor) and -0.4% [-0.95, 0.0] (reproducibility-aware); interaction null.

Allocation addendum 3 (post hoc): two thirds of the predictor effect comes from using both orientations of the other lines' history (S_both - S +4.4% [2.0, 6.8]); modelling the joint confirmation adds +2.1% [-1.6, +6.1], unresolved. S_both is therefore a registered information-matched comparator.

Phase 2 (EXPLORATORY): target-line feedback with a development-fitted lambda (0.26-0.30 role-swapped, 0.24-0.36 same-condition) improves squared error of the independent measurement slightly (-0.71 [-1.10, -0.34] of 44.3) but not the ordering of unpurchased candidates on role-swapped validation (concordance -0.0006 [-0.0020, +0.0008]); it is therefore NOT a factor here (stop rule: no added complexity without an action gain). It may enter only as the registered secondary arm F below, and only on a release with qualified same-condition repeats, where its ordering gain was +0.0065 [0.0029, 0.0101] on 14 lines.

requirements: complete design-defined menu per target line in which every candidate has a screen measurement and an independent verification measurement on disjoint plates from a different seeding event (date-stamped raw plate records with DATE_CREATED and CELL_ID or equivalent), same conditions or an explicitly declared, protocol-wide condition change
the other lines of the same tissue measured in both roles (history for predictor R and comparator S_both)
the authors' synergy rule and QC; plate identifiers; controls per plate documented

number of target lines n computed before opening from the line-level SD of the primary contrast (0.48 per line with two role assignments in development): n >= 150 lines with two role assignments (>= 250 with one) for a decision that can resolve tau = 5% in both directions at 80% power; if 45 <= n < 150 the run may proceed only as 'L > 0 or abstain' with that limitation registered
outcome columns never read before the freeze; design census receipt first
data_gate.refusal: DATA_NOT_QUALIFIED (named failing requirement) or INSUFFICIENT_UNITS; record the census and stop

budget_and_time.unit_primary: M = ceil(0.20 x menu) orientation measurements per line; every arm spends exactly M (paired: M - (M mod 2), remainder recorded as unavoidable)
budget_and_time.unit_secondary: W combination wells (14 x plates behind each orientation measurement); single-agent wells, control wells (raw Jaaks layout observed on all 3,106 plates: 6 untreated, 114 DMSO plus 0-38 DMSO-only positions, 28 blank, 34 MG-132, 34 staurosporine = 216-254; the screening documentation states 200) and custom-plate counts reported per arm and branch, not matched
budget_and_time.rounds: all four 2x2 cells: R = 4 decision rounds plus one verification-first terminal round (5 rounds, >= 20 days at the documented >= 4 days per round); baselines are run at their natural rounds and in time-matched secondary comparisons at 2 and 3 total rounds
budget_and_time.carry_over: unused capacity carries forward; round-R reserve sized from history screen-call probabilities; terminal round verifies first, leftover buys terminal screens reported separately
budget_and_time.unknown: prices per well and plate, labour, culture capacity and days beyond the 4-day assay minimum stay null

factors.predictor_S: static screen-label history: new screens ranked by the shrunk history mean of the screen-orientation label (k0 = 2); verification probabilities pooled (no pair-specific confirmation information)
factors.predictor_R: reproducibility-aware static history: new screens ranked by the shrunk history probability p_sv = P(screen call AND verification call) from other lines' both roles; p_v|s pair-specific (k0 = 2)
factors.scheduler_V: verify-hits with reserve and terminal round: every pending screen hit is verified first (highest screen label first), then new screens in predictor order
factors.scheduler_I: index scheduler: greedy by value per cost, verify value p_v|s / c_v vs screen value p_sv / c_s (under S: p_s x base / c_s and base / c_v), same reserve and terminal round

baselines.paired_full: both orientations of each ranked pair, full feasible budget (1 round natural)
baselines.fixed_split_dev: verification fraction f selected on development data only (leave-one-tissue-out on the development release; 0.30-0.40 on Jaaks)
baselines.S_both: information-matched static: rank by the history mean of (screen label + verification label)/2 under scheduler V
baselines.screen_only: zero-verification arm (observed confirmed = 0 by the reporting rule; hidden validated reported separately)
baselines.random_V: random ranking with scheduler V (20 seeds; zero arm for ranking)

secondary_arm_F: only if the release has qualified same-condition repeats: under scheduler V, rank new screens by the repeats workstream's U_lambda prediction V0 + lambda_U x F_U (V0 = shrunk history mean of the verification label; F_U = frozen TransferWorld posterior minus prior given the purchased screen labels; lambda_U = 0.27, median of the development folds, frozen now), against the same ranking with lambda = 0 (V0 alone), so the feedback contribution is isolated

endpoints.primary: independently confirmed discoveries per line actually obtained through paid measurements (screen call AND paid verification call); arm total = sum over lines; line value = mean over role assignments
reported_separately: missed discoveries (validated screen hits left unverified; validated pairs never screened)
resources by branch (orientation measurements, dose points, combination wells, custom plates, single-agent and control wells, native plates)

secondary_contrasts: time-matched comparisons at 2 and 3 total rounds

minimum_meaningful_gain.basis: review/statistics.json: with rounds and wells fixed the proposed arm adds ~0 wells, rounds and compute; 5% sits above accounting artefacts (odd-budget remainder ~1.5%, old avoidable underuse 4.95%) and the +2-3% screen-level gains that failed to transfer, and is ~1/7 of the attainable headroom; a judgement, no external requirement found. The historical 10% (fourfold latency against a one-round static arm) is NOT inherited, because verify-hits is itself multistage; the historical threshold and verdict remain unchanged in their own study.
minimum_meaningful_gain.absolute: about 0.10 confirmed discoveries per line at the development baseline (2.02 per line)

inference: stratified line bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed fixed at freeze) on per-line paired differences; two-way lines x pairs bootstrap as sensitivity; Bonferroni over the three registered 2x2 contrasts for any claim beyond the primary

decision_rules.SMALL: L > 0 and U < tau: adopt only if free at equal rounds and wells
decision_rules.UNRESOLVED: L <= 0 and U >= tau: abstain; not evidence of no effect

risk_statement: no certificate-based decision is part of this protocol; if one is added it is evaluated at one fixed time and reports P(act and wrong), not P(wrong | act)
llm_arm: none (review/llm_plan.json: DO_NOT_RUN; no specific decision contribution identified)
stopping: one opening per release; no interim looks; any rerun is a logged second opening

runner.dry_run: PYTHONPATH='src;.' python -m research.astra.reproducible_allocation_20261003.allocation.replay --dry <dir>; ... .allocation.addendum_2x2 --dry <dir> (both pass on a synthetic Jaaks-format release, 2026-10-04)
